title: Kholak (Tsampa with Butter Tea)
steps: Place roasted barley flour (tsampa) in a bowl.
Pour hot butter tea (or salted tea) over the flour.
Add a small piece of yak or cow butter if desired.
Knead the mixture with your fingers into a soft, edible dough.
Eat directly with your hands.

fullIngredients.name: 1–2 cups hot butter tea (or plain salted tea)
1–2 tsp yak or cow butter (optional extra)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditionally eaten any time of day; perfect trekking food.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Can be made with water or diluted chhang in some valleys for variation.

title: Khambir (Tagi) with Butter Tea
steps: Knead whole wheat flour, yeast, salt, and warm water into a soft dough.
Let the dough ferment and rise for a few hours.
Shape into thick, round breads.
Cook on a hot iron griddle, then roast directly over an open flame until crusty.
Serve warm with hot butter tea.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Keeps well for several days at room temperature.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Symbol of hospitality in Ladakhi homes.

title: Paba
steps: Boil water in a pot with a pinch of salt.
Slowly whisk in the mixed roasted flour (barley, wheat, buckwheat).
Stir continuously to prevent lumps until it forms a thick, dough-like consistency.
Cook for a few more minutes until done.
Serve hot with a dollop of ghee or butter.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Highly sustaining field food traditionally carried to work.

title: Vegetable Skyu
steps: Knead wheat flour and water into a stiff dough and shape into small thumb-sized pasta pieces.
Boil water or a light broth with diced carrots, turnips, and potatoes.
Add the shaped pasta (skyu) to the boiling broth.
Simmer until the pasta and vegetables are fully cooked.
Season with salt, pepper, and fresh herbs.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, ginger (optional traditional use is minimal)
Salt, black pepper, fresh herbs (cilantro, celery greens)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Sometimes made with milk (oma-skyu) for creamier version.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Root vegetables are traditional; omit for stricter diets.

title: Chutagi (Chhutagi)
steps: Knead wheat flour into a dough, roll out, and shape into distinctive 'bow-tie' pasta.
Prepare a rich vegetable soup with carrots, turnips, peas, and spinach.
Drop the chutagi pasta into the simmering soup.
Cook until the pasta is tender and the broth thickens slightly.
Serve hot in deep bowls.

fullIngredients.name: Carrots, turnips, potatoes, peas, spinach or local greens

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Often prepared during harvest season for energy.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Meat version with goat trotters exists for non-veg.

title: Vegetable Thukpa
steps: Prepare a flavorful vegetable broth using local greens, carrots, and onions.
Prepare fresh noodles or use dried noodles.
Add the noodles to the boiling broth.
Simmer until the noodles and vegetables are cooked.
Season with salt, pepper, and soy sauce if desired.

fullIngredients.name: Wheat or barley noodles (fresh or dried)
Carrots, cabbage, spinach or local greens

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Variants include thenthuk (hand-pulled) and gyathuk.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Widely available in Leh restaurants in both veg and non-veg forms.

title: Mutton Skyu
steps: Boil mutton pieces to create a rich meat broth.
Knead wheat flour and shape into small thumb-sized pasta pieces (skyu).
Add diced root vegetables to the mutton broth.
Drop the skyu pasta into the boiling broth.
Simmer until the pasta is cooked and absorbs the meaty flavor.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Ideal winter dish for warmth and calories.

title: Vegetable Momos (Mokmok)
steps: Prepare a smooth dough of wheat flour and water.
Finely chop cabbage, carrots, onions, and season with salt and pepper.
Roll dough into thin circles and place a spoonful of vegetable filling in the center.
Pleat and seal to form dumplings.
Steam for 10-15 minutes until fully cooked.

fullIngredients.name: Cabbage, carrot, onion, spinach or local greens

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Mokthuk is the version served in soup.

title: Mutton Momos
steps: Prepare a smooth dough of wheat flour and water.
Mix minced mutton with finely chopped onions, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Roll dough into thin circles and place the meat filling in the center.
Pleat and seal to form dumplings.
Steam for 15-20 minutes until the meat is thoroughly cooked.

fullIngredients.name: Salt, black pepper, a little oil

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Yak meat was traditional but is now restricted; mutton is the common substitute.

title: Yarkhandi Pulao
steps: Soak rice for 30 minutes.
Sauté onions, garlic, and mutton pieces in oil until browned.
Add julienned carrots and whole spices, then pour in water to make a broth.
Add the soaked rice and simmer.
Cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.

fullIngredients.name: Raisins, apricot kernels or dried apricots

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Rice was historically a luxury grain in the region.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Modern versions are less fatty than the traditional ones.

title: Tingmo (Timok) with Vegetable Stew
steps: Knead wheat flour, yeast, and water into a soft dough and let it ferment.
Roll the dough out, brush with a little oil, and fold into intricate bun shapes.
Let the shaped buns rest for a second rise.
Steam the buns for 15-20 minutes until fluffy and cooked.
Serve hot with stews or curries.

fullIngredients.name: Vegetable stew or dal for serving (contains onion, garlic)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Also eaten as a snack or with butter tea.

title: Steamed Vegetable Momos
steps: Prepare a basic dough and a savory filling (veg or meat).
Roll out small wrappers and fill them.
Seal the momos by crimping the edges.
Steam vigorously for 12-15 minutes.
Serve hot as a snack with fiery chili sauce.

fullIngredients.name: Cabbage, carrot, onion, spinach or local greens

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Ubiquitous snack; also available fried or in soup (mokthuk).

title: Khambir (Snack)
steps: Tear freshly baked or leftover khambir (local bread) into bite-sized pieces.
Serve the pieces on a platter.
Prepare a hot cup of butter tea or savory dip.
Dip the bread pieces into the tea or dip before eating.
Enjoy as a quick, sustaining afternoon snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Keeps for days; ideal travel food.

title: Gur Gur Chai (Butter Tea)
steps: Boil water with strong black tea leaves until a dark decoction forms.
Strain the tea into a traditional wooden churner (or modern blender).
Add a generous lump of yak butter (or cow butter) and salt.
Churn or blend vigorously until the tea becomes creamy and frothy.
Serve piping hot.

fullIngredients.name: Strong black or green tea leaves

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Acquired taste for most outsiders; essential for hydration and warmth at altitude.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often drunk throughout the day with khambir or tsampa.
